standouts.title: OpenAI DevDay: Dots, Agents & $100B Opportunities
standouts.summary: Greg Isenberg digested ~60 minutes of Sam Altman on stage at OpenAI DevDay 2026 into the four launches that matter for builders: Dots (always-on personal agents with their own cloud computer), the Decisions API (instant pick-one-answer calls), the Agents API with computer use, and Sign in with ChatGPT (users bring their own ChatGPT plan into third-party apps). The big picture: OpenAI is rebuilding the app/plugin ecosystem around ChatGPT's ~1.2 billion weekly users, with a first dot included in Pro and Business Premium plans.
args: Dots is OpenAI selling you an employee: always-on agents running GPT-6 Astra, each with its own cloud computer and browser, 4,000+ app integrations, working in ChatGPT, Slack and Teams (SMS coming). Enterprise specialist dots were previewed for accounting, marketing and legal — yes, accounting specifically.

Sign in with ChatGPT changes who pays for your users' tokens: a user's existing plan covers OpenAI usage inside third-party apps (16 launch partners), so a free core app with paid upsells now works, and plugins become full apps living inside ChatGPT.

The builder's framework: the strongest businesses in this world own the trigger, the action, and the feedback loop. Two open ideas he hopes someone takes: real-world work APIs (workflows too niche for OpenAI to build) and an analytics layer for agent discovery.
standouts.why: This is your lane at exactly the right moment. Two Alpha Infra plays: (a) implementation — OpenAI just created massive demand for dot/plugin configuration without creating the supply; firms need someone to wire their specialist dots into real workflows; (b) the analytics-for-agent-discovery idea maps straight onto data readiness (who owns the trigger, the action, the feedback). Note the tension: specialist dots for accounting is OpenAI eventually eating the workflow automation you sell, so position as the independent integrator, not a competitor. Content idea: LinkedIn post on what DevDay means for accounting and finance teams — most CFOs missed that ChatGPT now ships with an accountant-shaped dot.

standouts.title: Anthropic's Financials Revealed — The Losses Are Stunning
standouts.summary: Paul Kedrosky breaks down the leaked draft of Anthropic's S-1 (via Reuters): 2025 revenue of ~$4.6B (up 12x year over year), an $8B operating loss, a $42B net loss (mostly non-cash accounting charges), and $518B in future cloud and infrastructure commitments locked into non-cancellation agreements. Roughly 80 of the 261-page prospectus is risk factors, including warnings of "catastrophic or existential risks" from its own models. Jay Ritter then covers Oura shelving its $2.2B IPO as market jitters spread, and Ed closes on Manchester City being found guilty of all charges in the Premier League financial-breach case.
args: The AI lab unit economics are extreme: Anthropic's biggest cost is rented compute ($7.3B of $12.7B in 2025 operating expenses), and $518B in locked-in future commitments dwarfs $4.6B of revenue. The bet is that models keep scaling into the spend. It's targeting a >$2T valuation (private valuation was ~$965B in May) with a listing expected after the November midterms.

The most consequential disclosure is the risk section: a safety-first lab now warns in a sworn SEC filing that its own models could manipulate, conceal information, resist shutdown, or act in blackmail-like ways. The safety debate just moved from Twitter to the prospectus.

The IPO window is wobbling even for the good ones: Oura is profitable, has 5.7M paid members and ~90% revenue growth — and still pulled its listing (50M shares at $40–44, up to $2.2B) citing market uncertainty. When the profitable ones wait, everyone's waitlist moves.
standouts.why: Pure finance-reading practice, right in the CA toolkit. Two reusable frames: (a) Anthropic's $518B-in-commitments vs $4.6B-in-revenue is the extreme end of the capex bet your clients are debating at smaller scale — someone has to model the break case; (b) Oura's profitable patience vs Anthropic's spend-everything contrast makes a clean LinkedIn post: "two ways to price an AI bet." Question to surface, not advice: are clients' AI pilots Anthropic bets or Oura bets? Sports-business footnote from your MLC days: City's ~£900M in sham contracts over 2009–2018 is the largest financial-fair-play enforcement we've seen — sanctions pending, appeal due Oct 2.
